top_story: Iran’s reported strike on two tankers under U.S. escort in the Strait of Hormuz on 31 July widened the confrontation beyond military targets, jolting energy markets and exposing how quickly regional commerce and civilian livelihoods can be pulled into U.S.-Iran escalation. Trump’s 2 August decision to cancel planned strikes suggests both Washington and regional states are trying to contain a broader war, even after direct attacks tested deterrence and raised the cost of miscalculation. This de-escalatory turn sits against Gaza’s enduring reality, where the long-running conditions of death, denied recovery, and social devastation have continued into repeated family annihilation, underscored by Fatima Nofal’s loss of yet another son in central Gaza. The regional picture is one of leaders stepping back from one acute interstate crisis while Palestinians remain trapped in a chronic catastrophe that keeps reshaping civilian life faster than diplomacy can respond.
